# Independent audit of the actual constant-profile rectangle obstruction

Audited all six sections of `candidate b29a253caa27d987`. **PASS.** The result refutes an auxiliary absolute raw-depth target and, separately, a prescribed-center version of the weaker edge target. It does not refute OC or the existence form of the weaker edge target.

The endpoint rectangles have area one and centroid zero. Their exact midpoint rectangle has area 9/8; the convex hull across bases -1 and +1 has precisely these three integer fibers. At alpha=1/2 the left fiber contributes its supporting edge, of area zero, the right contributes 3/4, and the middle contributes 9/16. Thus the actual closed ambient cap has mass 21/16=4/3-1/48. Its positive boundary trace has not been confused with an empty set. The constant profiles reproduce the actual Minkowski midpoint, so this is also an exact one-piece profile counterexample.

The full width-family tail minimization correctly includes the proper interval, both saturation ranges, and R=1. Its value is R/8+3/4+5/(8R), minimized at sqrt(5), with the displayed factorization of the difference from 4/3. On the middle fiber, continuous reflection makes depth even, and halfspace-depth quasiconcavity makes the origin a maximizing point. On either extreme fiber a finite integer tilt isolates an ordinary cap of area at most 1/2. The same explicit upper bound therefore excludes the absolute target even after allowing an arbitrary center. This does not assert an exact global depth or an all-direction lower bound.

Eliminating R gives the stated actual-midpoint curve 3m/2-sqrt(m(m-1)); its comparison with (m+1)/3 has positive sides before squaring and the exact positive polynomial 13m^2+8m+4. The edge-credit interval calculations have the indicated constants.

For Section 6, the added left triangle has area 59/32 and lies wholly at s<=-3/4. Consequently the positive-s middle cap remains exactly 9/16 while the total middle area becomes 95/32. The same actual through-center cap has mass 126/96, below the requested edge credit 127/96. The bare middle-centroid bound is 95/72 and is short by 1/288. Those facts do not bound the actual depth at the middle centroid from above, as the source explicitly states. Since the enlarged middle contains the endpoint Minkowski midpoint, the final three-fiber convex hull has exactly the stated slices. Its ordinary OC target is indeed 53/48.

The obstruction is compatible with both the proved triangle-endpoint theorem and the six-piece reduction: constant profiles are already within that finite class, but the absolute 4/3 target is false there. Any continuation must use additional geometry, the actual middle mass, or an independently controlled center choice.

## Independent audit of the added exact middle-centroid calculation

Section 7 **passes**, with two requested captured/excluded wording repairs. Its exact ordinary centroid depth provides the desired credit for the specific pentagon of Section 6 and does not provide a universal compensation theorem.

The symmetry reduction to X+tY=g with t>=0 includes both sides of every nonhorizontal line; horizontal lines are treated separately. The three cut statuses in (9) are exhaustive because the moving lower intersection traverses the left slope, horizontal lower edge, and right vertical edge in that order, while the upper intersection stays on the left upper slope. The displayed middle-status quadrilateral is the captured polygon for E(t), and both lower vertices are captured in the last status. The source had called these excluded; the author has been asked to correct those labels. The formulas already have the correct captured-side signs.

The derivative signs and the last-status maximizing tilt are correct. In the stipulated w range, w/2<g<1 and 0<2g-w<1, so the unique positive critical tilt lies in the stated last status. The exact identity (11) proves both that the complementary-side minimum is at least g^2 and that the horizontal half-area is at least g^2. Thus the asserted depth is genuinely over all ordinary halfspaces, attained by the apex-side cap.

The affine map of the actual pentagon has inverse Jacobian 59/32 and sends it exactly to P_(77/59). Its centroid and all three rational depth/surplus values in (12) check. A nonvertical ambient cap restricts to an ordinary containing halfplane of the middle fiber; a vertical cap contains that whole fiber. Hence the ordinary depth is a valid lower bound for the actual mixed depth at this specified point. The full updated verifier passes **32,115 exact checks**.

## Added Section 8: the mass-dependent one-apex family

**PASS.** The larger w range keeps g<1 and all three line statuses unchanged, while retaining the minimum of the two competing cap values instead of using (11). Thus (13) follows from the already audited all-normal calculation.

For the indicated rectangle plus one apex, the appended triangle has area k-m. Normalizing it to the unit triangular part of P_w gives exactly w=1+m/[2(k-m)], with inverse area factor k-m. The stipulated rectangle of mass parameters implies w<=27/19, within the proved status range. Substitution gives both rational entries of (16); in particular 2g-w=(2k+m)/(6k), which independently checks the second entry. The numerators in (17) and their partial derivatives are correct. The lower bound on the k derivative of N1 uses k<=3 only after applying the uniform negative bound -8/3, so its direction is valid even where that factor is positive. Both positive corner values are exact.

Finally, failure of the displayed axial credit with k<=3 implies J_R<4/3 and hence 5/3<R<3. This bounds m_R<=4/3, and the exact minimum of J_R gives k>(5+3sqrt(5))/4>35/12. Therefore the mass-dependent ordinary-centroid theorem pays every obstruction of this stated axial one-apex form. It does not replace an arbitrary compatible K by that family. The updated verifier passes **32,125 exact checks**.

The two earlier captured/excluded labels have now been corrected in the source.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
